title: Democrat Rob Sand wins Iowa’s gubernatorial race as party plans rebuild
summary: Sand, auditor for state with strong Trump support, defeats Maha-backed Republican Zach Lahn as Democrats win big

blocks.text: Democrat Rob Sand has been elected governor of Iowa, the Associated Press projects, a milestone as his party seeks to rebuild its political standing in the midwestern state.

Sand, the state auditor who is the sole Democrat holding statewide office in Iowa, triumphed over Republican Zach Lahn, a political newcomer backed by Robert F Kennedy Jr’s “Make America healthy again” movement.

The victory is significant for Democrats in Iowa, which twice backed Barack Obama but has voted for Trump all three times he was on the presidential ballot, while Republicans have come to dominate state politics. Sand is the first Democrat to win the governor’s office since 2006.

Sand’s victory comes as Democrats netted historic wins in gubernatorial elections nationwide, including in states where they have struggled in recent years. In Georgia, former Atlanta mayor Keisha Lance Bottoms has become the first Black woman elected governor in the country.
Sand, 44, is a native Iowan who has cast himself as a unifier who would restore balance to the state’s politics.
“To Iowa Democrats, we’ve had a hard few years here in Iowa, but balanced government has been restored,” Sand said at his victory party on Tuesday night as the crowd cheered.

He had the crowd sing America the Beautiful together, a feature of his hundreds of town halls as he criss-crossed the state. He thanked the state’s voters, and emphasized how he intends to bring people to the table to improve water quality, accountability and the political process.
“Come January, we will be forced to work together,” he said of the political parties, later adding: “Left wing, right wing, same bird.”

Sand had been leading in the polls ahead of election day. Lahn, who won the Republican primary over a candidate endorsed by Donald Trump, had been accused by Iowa Democrats of spending a disproportionate amount of time in Kansas, despite wanting to be governor of Iowa. The New York Times reported in October that although Lahn voted in Iowa in the 2024 general election, he had his ballot mailed to him in Kansas.
Lahn had also faced scrutiny for his complicated ties to the Koch family, the Republican billionaire mega-donors.
An emphasis on bipartisan, balanced politics had been a hallmark of Sands’s campaign, with a focus on the need to return to Iowa as a “commonsense state”.
“I think a big piece of that was because we elected both Democrats and Republicans, and they had to work together to get anything done,” Sand said at a rally on 28 October.
“We have had 10 years of one-party control in the state of Iowa, and that is what led us to where we are today.”
His parents, Kevin and Leslie, knocked doors for him – his mom more than his dad. “His mother has worked much harder than I,” Kevin Sand said.
Asked how she felt about Rob’s win, Leslie said: “Proud, excited, elated, glad it’s over. Proud, proud, proud.”
And, his parents added, they’re thrilled for Iowa.
“I’m so happy for Iowa because he’s going to do a great job doing the very best he can to turn things around and get them to where they need to be,” Kevin said.

At his victory party, Carol Sand, Rob’s aunt, said that as a public school teacher, she was relieved that her nephew – a product of the public education system himself – would be in the governor’s office.
“He’s going to right the ship in Iowa and bring some accountability,” Carol Sand said.
Rachel Leingang contributed reporting
